Subject: ACME - Reranking model fit & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Jordan — great context on the query distributions and the user-facing quality goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: improve search relevance with a reranking layer while keeping latency <= 120ms p50 for first-pass + rerank on our Dedicated configuration.
- Dataset: shared sample (1.2k queries + candidate pools) that you uploaded to the drive link below.
- Recommended starting models: redwood-rerank-4b-quant (best accuracy/cost tradeoff) and redwood-rerank-1b (fast, lower-cost baseline).
- Evaluation plan: run NDCG@10 and MRR on your prompt set, verify no quality regressions vs current production baseline. Target: NDCG@10 >= 0.82 and MRR >= 0.60 for rollout.

Next steps:
1) I attached our prompt set and a short benchmark harness you can run locally: prompt_set_acme_v1.json (see attachment).
2) We'll run an initial validation on a 10% sample and share NDCG/MRR results + recommended config.
3) If results are promising, propose an A/B with 5-10% traffic for two weeks to measure downstream metrics (CTR, conversion).

Attachments: [Attachment: prompt_set_acme_v1.json (application/json)]
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-rerank-benchmarks

Thanks — I'll kick off the run on our side once you confirm the dataset snapshot to use.

Marissa

Great questions — answers below: 

1) Evaluation pools: yes, our NDCG/MRR numbers are computed on the full candidate pools you provided. We'll also report truncated variants (top-100) for parity with any downstream caches.
2) Model selection rationale: redwood-rerank-4b-quant gives ~6-8% higher NDCG vs the 1b baseline on similar e-comm workloads we've run, with ~2x cost vs 1b but still within your Dedicated budget. Long-query regression: we ran a quick slice on queries >75 tokens and saw a small drop (~1.5 NDCG points) on the 4b-quant candidate; we include that slice in the report and can tune prompts/temperature.
3) Security: for >10k exports we recommend using VPC/private upload (or scrub PII) — happy to loop Security. If you will share the 50k snapshot, please indicate whether data is scrubbed.

I've run an initial validation on a 10% sample (attached). Summary: NDCG@10 = 0.79, MRR = 0.58 for the 4b-quant vs your current baseline of NDCG@10 = 0.76, MRR = 0.55. So we see improvement but not yet at your target. Attached: acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.csv and a short PDF summary.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.csv (text/csv)], [Attachment: benchmark_results_summary.pdf (application/pdf)]
Links: https://docs.redwood.com/playbooks/reranking-validation

Suggested next steps:
- Run full-sample validation (we can do this on Dedicated infra) and try the following knobs: prompt engineering (two prompt variants included), candidate-score calibration, and lightweight feature augmentation (click priors).
- If the full-sample run shows NDCG >=0.82, we recommend a staged A/B (5% -> 10%) for two weeks with monitoring on CTR, conversion, latency, and negative-feedback rate.

Let me know if you want us to run the full-sample job from our side (we can pull from your drive link with a signed NDA/transfer).

Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Quick update from our reproducibility run (results attached and summarized):

- Setup: reproduced Marissa's 10% run on Dedicated (same model snapshots). Also ran full-sample (50k) on redwood-rerank-1b and redwood-rerank-4b-quant.
- Key metrics (full sample):
  - redwood-rerank-1b: NDCG@10 = 0.789, MRR = 0.592
  - redwood-rerank-4b-quant: NDCG@10 = 0.824, MRR = 0.605
- Long-query slice (>75 tokens): 4b-quant shows a small dip vs 1b (NDCG delta ~ -0.012). We saw improved results when applying the "prompt-variant-b" which adds candidate context to the prompt.
- Latency: 4b-quant p50 rerank = 110ms (within their 120ms target), p95 = 240ms. We should monitor p95 at scale.

Recommendation and A/B plan:
- Candidate config: use redwood-rerank-4b-quant with prompt-variant-b + cheap feature augmentation (click priors).
- A/B: start at 5% user traffic for 2 weeks, monitor NDCG proxy metrics + business KPIs (CTR, conversion). If uplift >= +3% CTR and no negative-feedback spikes and latency p95 < 300ms, expand to 20% for another 2 weeks.
- Rollout guardrails: automatic rollback if negative-feedback rate increases >0.5% absolute or latency p95 exceeds 400ms for >1 hour.

I'll attach the run CSV and a short summary that we can share with Jordan (acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_v1.csv, benchmark_results_summary.pdf). Let me know if you want me to draft the A/B playbook for ACME.

Dylan
